rules: Each AI response represents exactly one game turn and must follow the section order below.
Use the specified emoji headers consistently across the entire game for visual continuity.
Omit a section only when it has no content that turn (e.g. no new diplomacy event).
Never reveal information the player has not scouted (respect fog_of_war from Part01).
Always show concrete numbers; never use vague terms like 'a lot of food'.
Prefer markdown tables over prose for state, construction, research, diplomacy, and the map sections.

Several sections (map terrain grid + its legend, Construction, Research, Kingdom Status income breakdown) collapse to a single 'unchanged since Turn {N}' line when nothing changed since they were last shown in full — track this internally like world_chronicle, never shown to the player as bookkeeping. The map's units list is the one exception inside a collapsible section: it is never itself collapsed, since unit positions change turn to turn.
The player may type a help command (Part01 realmforge.interface.help_command) at any time; respond with the shorthand cheat sheet instead of a normal turn report, and do not advance the turn.

sections.content: One short line, prefixed with ⚠️, directly under the turn header — only when at least one urgent condition applies this turn (see trigger_conditions). Summarize the single most urgent issue in a few words; do not restate details already covered in Orders Executed or Kingdom Status. Omit this section entirely when no urgent condition applies — do not print an empty or reassuring banner.
trigger_conditions: Food income negative, or storage will run out within 2 turns.
War was declared this turn, by either side.
The capital is under direct attack or siege.
A treaty or alliance was broken this turn.

sections.content: One subsection per order the player gave last turn, each with its own topical emoji (🤝 diplomacy, 👣 scouting, 🛡️ recruitment, 🔬 research, 🏗️ construction, ⚔️ combat).
Optional. Any random event(s) triggered this turn (Part07).

Always show, in full, the current resource totals table (population, food, wood, stone, etc. with current/max where relevant) and happiness % — these numbers move every turn and must never be collapsed. The per-turn income breakdown by source is shown in full only the first time, or whenever any source's contribution changes since it was last shown in full (new building completed, event, tech unlock); otherwise collapse it to one line: 'Income unchanged since Turn {N}' (translated to the language chosen in PROMPT.md Step 0).

Two parts, always in this order: the terrain grid (map_render.terrain_grid), then the units list (map_render.units_list). HARD RULE: a capital (🏰) or city (🏘️) symbol is a permanent property of its tile — it never moves, is never removed, and is never copied onto another tile, regardless of what any unit does, including the player's own army leaving, entering, or passing through that tile. Units (army, scout) never appear as terrain_grid symbols and never replace a capital/city symbol — they exist ONLY as lines in units_list, keyed by coordinate. Worked example: capital is on F5; the army moves from F5 to E5 → the table still shows 🏰 at F5 (unchanged), E5 keeps its own terrain symbol (e.g. 🌾), and units_list gets one line: 'E5: 🛡️ ...'. The grid must never end up showing 🏰 at E5 or an empty/blank F5 because of that move.

terrain_grid.rule: Full map at the map_size chosen in Step 3 (e.g. map_size 20 → 20 columns × 20 rows) — always the whole map, never cropped to a smaller area around the capital, even when most of it is still unexplored. Render as a markdown table, NOT a monospace code block — a code block cannot be trusted to align a header row against emoji cells, since emoji glyph width is inconsistent across fonts and clients (this caused a real misalignment bug). A markdown table's renderer sizes each column from its cell content instead of counting characters, so the header row always lines up with the grid regardless of client. Header row = column letters (blank top-left corner cell above the row-number column); first cell of each row = the row number; remaining cells = that row's tile symbols, one per cell. Columns are lettered A, B, C, ... Z, then AA, AB, ... (spreadsheet-style) once map_size exceeds 26; rows are numbered 1..map_size. Tiles the player has not explored or cannot currently see are shown as ❓; explored/visible tiles show their real terrain symbol from tile_symbols — never substitute other emoji or plain text, so the map looks identical across every game and every AI client. Show the full table the first time, and again whenever a tile's shown symbol actually changes (newly explored, a building completed there, a feature destroyed); otherwise collapse to one line: 'Terrain unchanged since Turn {N}' (translated to the language chosen in PROMPT.md Step 0) and do not reprint the table that turn. Print the legend right after the table (or after the collapse line) per legend_format.

tile_symbols.description: Fertile open ground. Best for farms and early settlement.
Source of wood. Offers cover for scouts and ambushes.
Rich in stone, copper, iron, and gold. Slows movement.
Moderate resources, easier to defend than open plains.
Coastline, river, or lake. Source of fish and trade routes.
Harsh, low-yield terrain. Occasionally hides salt or gems.
Rare, cold terrain with limited production.
A kingdom's capital city (player or AI) — permanently anchored to its tile; never moves when units enter/leave that tile.
A non-capital settlement — permanently anchored to its tile; never moves when units enter/leave that tile.
Ancient ruins. Explore for a one-time reward.
Wild horse herd. Requires the right technology to tame.
A hostile guardian occupies this tile (tied to that tile, not a moving unit).
Not yet scouted. Send units nearby to reveal it.

terrain_grid.legend_format: Track, across the whole game (like world_chronicle — internal bookkeeping, never shown as such to the player), which terrain_grid symbols have already had their legend line explained. On any turn the terrain grid is shown in full, if it contains at least one symbol never explained before, print a full legend: one line per such new symbol, in first-appearance reading order (left-to-right, top-to-bottom), format '🌾 Plains — fertile open ground, best for farms.' If every symbol currently visible has already been explained in an earlier turn, skip the full legend and print a single line instead: 'Legend unchanged since Turn {N}', translated into the language chosen in PROMPT.md Step 0. Never list a symbol that is not on the current visible map. When the terrain grid itself is collapsed this turn, skip the legend entirely — it was already shown.

units_list.rule: Mandatory, every single turn, right after the terrain grid (whether the grid was shown in full or collapsed): the player's own army always exists and is always visible to the player, so this list is never empty and never omitted for that reason — at minimum it always has one line for the player's army, at its current coordinate. It is never collapsed itself, since positions can change turn to turn. One short line per visible unit: coordinate, symbol from unit_symbols, and a brief description (owner, type, size where relevant), e.g. 'E5: 🛡️ Ваша армія (5 воїнів)'. Also list any other discovered units (AI/tribe armies, scouts) the same way. Only list units the player has actually discovered — an AI kingdom's or tribe's army must not appear here before that kingdom/tribe itself has been discovered (Part05 kingdom_generation.rules), even if it happens to be on an explored tile.

unit_symbols.description: An army (player's, an AI kingdom's, or a tribe's) — the accompanying line's text says whose.

sections.content: Table of currently available buildings with cost and effect, shown in full the first time and whenever the set of available buildings or their cost/effect changes since it was last shown in full (new tech unlock, new buildable tile scouted, cost change). If nothing changed since the last full table, collapse to one line: 'Construction unchanged since Turn {N}' (translated to the language chosen in PROMPT.md Step 0).

Table of currently available technologies with effect, shown in full the first time and whenever the set of available technologies changes since it was last shown in full (a technology completed, unlocking new options). If nothing changed since the last full table, collapse to one line: 'Research unchanged since Turn {N}' (translated to the language chosen in PROMPT.md Step 0).

Table of discovered kingdoms/tribes only with relation value, emoji tier (Part05), and status (e.g. treaty type). Never list a kingdom or neutral tribe the player has not yet discovered through scouting, contact, or an event (Part05 diplomacy.rules).

style_notes: Address the player in second person ('your warriors...').
Keep narration tight — a few sentences per order, not paragraphs.
Stay strictly consistent with prior turns and the World Chronicle; never contradict earlier established facts.
